name: RECOVERY_AUTHORITY
cause: no adjudicated authority for recovery decisions
wal.lisp resolves PREPARED by assumption at recovery start
wal_triad_bridge.py refuses to resolve IN_DOUBT without an explicit frame
impact: CON-INV-07 cannot be satisfied while both surfaces exist
recovery outcome depends on which surface runs
replay and canonical effect can diverge after a crash
dependency: then re-run the crash-recovery test against the adopted rule
resolution: adjudicate which surface holds recovery authority; no winner can be assigned from the corpus
blocked_by: authority_conflict (wal.lisp resolves at recovery start, bridge is fail-closed)
sequenced_actions: re-classify code#03 vs code#05 under adopted authority
repair wal.lisp recovery to preserve IN_DOUBT instead of ABORT-by-assumption
re-run crash-recovery test against adopted rule

adoption.decision: RECOVERY_AUTHORITY = wal_triad_bridge fail-closed IN_DOUBT retention; wal.lisp start-of-recovery ABORT resolution is a violation pending repair
adoption.adopted_rule: PREPARED transactions are never resolved by assumption at recovery start. Unresolved transactions stay IN_DOUBT — isolated, never canonical, never in the replay set — until an explicit resolution frame (COMMITTED or ABORTED) arrives.

name: WAL_TAIL_POLICY
cause: storage norm for partial tail records never adopted
implementation asserts truncation as the recovery operation
impact: any append-only claim that depends on the tail is unclassifiable
test corpus encodes the unadopted decision
dependency: then decide whether the existing test is a violation or a specification of the norm
resolution: adopt an explicit storage norm for incomplete records at recovery, or retract the test expectation
blocked_by: norm exists as a design claim only; implementation (code#02) contradicts it; implementation != adoption
sequenced_actions: make code#02 truncation conditional on an adopted norm (default: quarantine)
reconcile tests/test_cae_e2e.py expectation with the adopted norm

adoption.decision: WAL_TAIL_POLICY = quarantine (preserve partial tail records, exclude from canonical replay); truncation forbidden without an explicitly adopted norm plus recorded evidence
adoption.adopted_rule: Incomplete records at recovery are quarantined, never truncated. Truncation requires an explicitly adopted storage norm and recorded evidence; the existing truncation behaviour is a violation pending repair.

name: DURABILITY_NORM
cause: durability definition left open in the design
code#01 defines it as fdatasync success
code asserts precedence via its local tx table without a Canonical History comparison path
impact: durability claim is implementation-defined, not adopted
linearization-point claim is VERIFIED only under the unadopted definition
dependency: then build the Canonical History join path for precedence semantics
resolution: define durability precedence against Canonical History; code#06 satisfies only the txid/duplicate half of the claim
blocked_by: no Canonical History surface exists in the code corpus; the structural half of the claim has no join path
sequenced_actions: re-verify code#01 against the adopted norm
build Canonical-History join path for precedence semantics
lift restriction only after join path verified

adoption.decision: DURABILITY_NORM = fdatasync success of a fully written record as the local linearization point; Canonical-History precedence restricted to local scope until a join path exists
adoption.adopted_rule: Durability = successful fdatasync of a fully written record (append-and-sync). Precedence against Canonical History is not adopted: transaction-index claims hold in local scope only until a Canonical-History comparison path exists.

name: SURFACE_DIVERGENCE
cause: two independent implementation surfaces for the same state semantics
impact: no VERIFIED status can be assigned to the divergent nodes until authority is fixed
dependency: adjudication must precede any classification change
resolution: cannot be resolved here: no adjudicated authority; classification stays frozen (no win/lose)
blocked_by: hard constraint authority_conflict — two surfaces encode opposite rules for the same state semantics
sequenced_actions: repair wal.lisp to adopted norms or mark it legacy explicitly

adoption.decision: PRECEDENCE RULE = wal_triad_bridge is canonical authority for transaction/state semantics; runtime/phase-d/wal.lisp is a legacy physical WAL surface, non-authoritative for canonical state until aligned with ADR-001/ADR-002
adoption.adopted_rule: When implementation surfaces diverge on the same state semantics, the fail-closed bridge is authoritative. The wal.lisp recovery path is legacy and non-authoritative until repaired to the adopted norms.
